items.exampleAf: Ek koop brood by die winkel.
items.exampleEn: I buy bread at the shop.
I eat an egg for breakfast.
Mom is making chicken for supper.

items.exampleAf: Die boerewors is op die braai.
items.exampleEn: The boerewors is on the braai.

items.exampleAf: Pa eet biltong by die rugby.
items.exampleEn: Dad eats biltong at the rugby.

items.note: A plaited, syrup-soaked fried pastry.

items.exampleAf: Gee vir my die sout, asseblief.
Ons eet koek op my verjaarsdag.
items.exampleEn: We eat cake on my birthday.
The children are eating ice cream.

items.exampleAf: Te veel lekkergoed is sleg vir jou.
items.exampleEn: Too many sweets are bad for you.

items.exampleAf: Ek drink koffie in die oggend.
items.exampleEn: I drink coffee in the morning.
I eat an apple every day.

items.note: The fruit. The colour is 'oranje'.
Singular: druif.

items.exampleAf: Ek hou van aarbeie met room.

items.note: Also means 'root'.
Singular: ertjie.

items.exampleEn: What are we having for lunch?

items.note: Also the verb 'to grill'.

items.af: Ouma het die deeg in die yskas gesit sodat dit stadig kon rys.
items.en: Grandma put the dough in the fridge so that it could rise slowly.
wrongEn: Grandma put the dough in the oven so that it could rise slowly.
Grandma put the dough in the fridge because it had risen slowly.
Grandma put the dough in the fridge so that it could not rise.
Grandma will put the dough in the fridge so it can rise slowly.
wrongAf: Ouma het die deeg in die yskas gesit sodat kon dit stadig rys.
Ouma het die deeg in die yskas gesit omdat dit stadig gerys het.
Ouma het die deeg in die yskas gesit sodat dit stadig kon gerys.
Ouma het die deeg in die oond gesit sodat dit stadig kon rys.
items.note: 'Sodat' (so that) gives a purpose and sends the verbs last: sodat dit stadig kon rys.

items.af: Wanneer die kole wit gloei, kan ons die tjops opsit.
items.en: When the coals glow white, we can put the chops on.
wrongEn: When the coals glow red, we can put the chops on.
Before the coals glow white, we can put the chops on.
When the coals glow white, we can't put the chops on yet.
When the coals glowed white, we put the chops on.
wrongAf: Wanneer die kole gloei wit, kan ons die tjops opsit.
Wanneer die kole wit gloei, ons kan die tjops opsit.
Voordat die kole wit gloei, kan ons die tjops opsit.
Wanneer die kole rooi gloei, kan ons die tjops opsit.
items.note: 'Wanneer' (when) sends 'gloei' to the end; the main clause then starts with its verb: kan ons.

items.af: Die restaurant waarvan almal so hoog opgee, het ons teleurgestel.
items.en: The restaurant everyone speaks so highly of disappointed us.
wrongEn: The restaurant everyone complains about surprised us.
The restaurant everyone speaks so highly of did not disappoint us.
We disappointed the restaurant everyone speaks so highly of.
The restaurant everyone speaks so highly of will disappoint us.
wrongAf: Die restaurant waarvan almal so hoog gee op, het ons teleurgestel.
Die restaurant waarvan almal so hoog opgee, het ons geteleurstel.
Die restaurant waaroor almal kla, het ons verras.
Ons het die restaurant waarvan almal so hoog opgee, teleurgestel.
items.note: 'Hoog opgee van' = speak highly of, so 'van' becomes 'waarvan'. Separable 'opgee' stays whole at the end.

items.af: Die melktert is deur my klein boetie gebak, sonder Ma se hulp.
items.en: The milk tart was baked by my little brother, without Mom's help.
wrongEn: The milk tart was baked for my little brother, without Mom's help.
My little brother ate the milk tart, without Mom's help.
The milk tart was baked by my little brother, with Mom's help.
The milk tart is being baked by my little brother, without Mom's help.
wrongAf: Die melktert het deur my klein boetie gebak, sonder Ma se hulp.
Die melktert word deur my klein boetie gebak, sonder Ma se hulp.
Die melktert is vir my klein boetie gebak, sonder Ma se hulp.
Die melktert is deur my klein boetie bak, sonder Ma se hulp.
items.note: Past passive: is gebak (was baked), with 'deur' for the doer. 'Het gebak' would make it active.

items.af: Die kelner het gevra of ons voor tienuur nog iets wou bestel.
items.en: The waiter asked whether we wanted to order anything else before ten.
wrongEn: We asked the waiter whether we could order anything else before ten.
The waiter said that we could not order anything else after ten.
The waiter asked whether we wanted to order anything else after ten.
The waiter asked whether we wanted to order anything else before two.
wrongAf: Die kelner het gevra of wou ons voor tienuur nog iets bestel.
Ons het die kelner gevra of ons voor tienuur nog iets kon bestel.
Die kelner het gevra of ons voor twaalfuur nog iets wou bestel.
Die kelner het gevra of ons na tienuur nog iets wou bestel.
items.note: Reported question with 'of' (whether): wou bestel goes last. Clock times are one word: tienuur.

items.af: Ons het nêrens 'n winkel gekry wat Sondagaand brood verkoop nie.
items.en: We found no shop anywhere that sold bread on Sunday evening.
wrongEn: We easily found a shop that sold bread on Sunday evening.
We found no shop anywhere that sold milk on Sunday morning.
We found no shop anywhere that didn't sell bread on Sunday evening.
We won't find a shop anywhere that sells bread on Sunday evening.
wrongAf: Ons het nêrens 'n winkel gekry wat Sondagaand brood verkoop.
Ons het nêrens 'n winkel gekry wat verkoop Sondagaand brood nie.
Ons het nêrens 'n winkel gekry wat Sondagaand brood geverkoop nie.
Ons het maklik 'n winkel gekry wat Sondagaand brood verkoop.
items.note: 'Nêrens ... nie' = nowhere. The closing 'nie' waits until after the relative clause 'wat ... verkoop'.

items.af: Geen gas het die sous geproe nie, want dit was glo vuurwarm.
items.en: No guest tasted the sauce: apparently it was fiery hot.
wrongEn: Every guest tasted the sauce: apparently it was fiery hot.
No guest liked the sauce: apparently it was fiery hot.
One guest tasted the sauce: apparently it was fiery hot.
No guest tasted the sauce: apparently it was very mild.
wrongAf: Geen gas het die sous geproe, want dit was glo vuurwarm.
Geen gas het die sous proe nie, want dit was glo vuurwarm.
Geen gas het die sous geproe nie, want dit glo vuurwarm was.
Elke gas het die sous geproe, want dit was glo vuurwarm.
items.note: 'Geen ... nie' = no (not any). 'Want' (because) keeps normal order, unlike 'omdat'. Proe (taste) becomes geproe.

items.af: Nadat ons ure lank gekook het, het die kinders alles opgeëet.
items.en: After we had cooked for hours, the children ate everything up.
wrongEn: After the children had cooked for hours, we ate everything up.
After we had cooked for hours, the children didn't eat a thing.
After we cook for hours, the children will eat everything up.
After we had cooked for hours, the children threw everything away.
wrongAf: Nadat ons ure lank gekook het, het die kinders alles geopeet.
Nadat ons ure lank gekook het, die kinders het alles opgeëet.
Nadat ons ure lank gekook het, het die kinders alles opeet.
Nadat die kinders ure lank gekook het, het ons alles opgeëet.
items.note: opeet becomes opgeëet: ge- goes after 'op', and the diaeresis (ë) shows a new syllable starts.

items.af: Jy moes die koek nie so lank gebak het nie; nou is dit pikswart.
items.en: You shouldn't have baked the cake so long; now it's pitch-black.
wrongEn: You didn't bake the cake long enough; now it's pitch-black.
You should have baked the cake longer; now it's raw.
You shouldn't bake the cake so long, or it will be pitch-black.
You had to bake the cake so long; now it's golden-brown.
wrongAf: Jy moes die koek nie so lank gebak het; nou is dit pikswart.
Jy moes die koek nie so lank bak het nie; nou is dit pikswart.
Jy moes die koek nie so lank gebak het nie; nou dit is pikswart.
Jy moes die koek langer gebak het; nou is dit rou.
items.note: moes + ge- + het = should have: moes ... gebak het. With 'nie' it means shouldn't have.

items.af: Ek het suiker met sout verwar, en nou is die pap gekrap.
items.en: I confused sugar with salt, and now the damage is done.
wrongEn: I confused sugar with salt, and now the porridge is stirred.
I confused salt with sugar, but no harm was done.
I mixed sugar with salt, and now the porridge is burnt.
I nearly confused sugar with salt, but caught it in time.
wrongAf: Ek het suiker met sout verwar, en nou die pap is gekrap.
Ek het suiker met sout geverwar, en nou is die pap gekrap.
Ek het suiker met sout verwar, en nou word die pap gekrap.
Ek het suiker met sout verwar, maar die pap is nie gekrap nie.
items.note: 'Nou is die pap gekrap' = now the damage is done (literally: now the porridge has been stirred).

items.af: Die ketel het op die stoof staan en fluit, asof dit ons roep.
items.en: The kettle stood whistling on the stove, as if it were calling us.
wrongEn: The kettle stood quietly on the stove, as if it were waiting for us.
The kettle stood whistling on the stove, because we were calling it.
We stood whistling at the kettle on the stove, as if calling it.
The kettle stood whistling on the stove, as if it were mocking us.
wrongAf: Die ketel het op die stoof staan en fluit, asof dit roep ons.
Die ketel het stil op die stoof gestaan, asof dit vir ons wag.
Die ketel het op die stoof staan en fluit, asof ons dit roep.
Die ketel het op die stoof staan en fluit, omdat ons dit roep.
items.note: Personification: the kettle calls like a person. 'Het staan en fluit' = stood whistling (no ge-).

items.af: Elke Saterdagoggend koop ons tuisgebakte brood by die boeremark.
items.en: Every Saturday morning we buy home-baked bread at the farmers' market.
wrongEn: Every Sunday morning we buy home-baked bread at the farmers' market.
Every Saturday we sell home-baked bread at the farmers' market.
Last Saturday we bought home-baked bread at the farmers' market.
Every Saturday morning we buy stale bread at the farmers' market.
wrongAf: Elke Saterdagoggend ons koop tuisgebakte brood by die boeremark.
Elke Saterdagoggend verkoop ons tuisgebakte brood by die boeremark.
Elke Sondagoggend koop ons tuisgebakte brood by die boeremark.
Elke Saterdagoggend koop ons tuisgebak brood by die boeremark.
items.note: A time phrase first pushes the verb before the subject: koop ons. Before a noun: tuisgebakte brood.

items.af: As die sjef die vis korter gebraai het, sou dit sag en sappig gebly het.
items.en: If the chef had fried the fish for less time, it would have stayed soft and juicy.
wrongEn: Because the chef fried the fish for less time, it stayed soft and juicy.
If the chef had fried the fish for longer, it would have stayed soft and juicy.
If the chef had fried the fish for less time, it would have gone dry and tough.
If the chef fries the fish for less time, it will stay soft and juicy.
wrongAf: As die sjef die vis korter gebraai het, dit sou sag en sappig gebly het.
As die sjef die vis korter het gebraai, sou dit sag en sappig gebly het.
As die sjef die vis korter gebraai het, sou dit sag en sappig bly het.
Omdat die sjef die vis korter gebraai het, het dit sag en sappig gebly.
items.note: Unreal past: as ... gebraai het, sou ... gebly het (if ... had fried, ... would have stayed).

items.af: Toe dit aan die lig kom dat die sap vervals is, is alles van die rakke verwyder.
items.en: When it came out that the juice was adulterated, it was all pulled from the shelves.
wrongEn: When it came out that the juice was adulterated, it was all put back on the shelves.
When it came out that the juice was pure, it was all pulled from the shelves.
Once it was all pulled from the shelves, it came out that the juice was adulterated.
When it came out that the juice was adulterated, only some was pulled.
wrongAf: Toe dit aan die lig kom dat die sap vervals is, alles is van die rakke verwyder.
Toe dit aan die lig kom dat die sap vervals is, het alles van die rakke verwyder.
Toe dit aan die lig kom dat die sap is vervals, is alles van die rakke verwyder.
Toe dit aan die lig kom dat die sap vervals is, is alles van die rakke geverwyder.
items.note: Two past passives (vervals is, is verwyder). 'Aan die lig kom' = come to light. Ver- verbs take no ge-.

items.af: Die gasvryheid waarvoor die Karoo bekend is, het ons heeltemal oorweldig.
items.en: The hospitality the Karoo is known for completely overwhelmed us.
wrongEn: The hospitality the Karoo is known for completely disappointed us.
The hospitality the Karoo is known for left us completely cold.
We completely overwhelmed the Karoo with our hospitality.
The hospitality the Karoo was once known for will overwhelm us.
wrongAf: Die gasvryheid waarvan die Karoo bekend is, het ons heeltemal oorweldig.
Die gasvryheid waarvoor die Karoo is bekend, het ons heeltemal oorweldig.
Die gasvryheid waarvoor die Karoo bekend is, het ons heeltemal geoorweldig.
Die gasvryheid waarvoor die Karoo bekend is, het ons heeltemal teleurgestel.
items.note: 'Bekend vir' (known for) becomes 'waarvoor' ('bekend om' gives 'waarom'). Oorweldig is stressed on -wel-, so no ge-.

items.af: Die inspekteur het gewaarsku dat die kombuis gesluit sou word indien dit vuil bly.
items.en: The inspector warned that the kitchen would be closed if it stayed dirty.
wrongEn: The inspector warned that the kitchen would be closed even if it was cleaned.
The owner warned that the kitchen would be closed if it stayed dirty.
The inspector said that the kitchen had been closed because it was dirty.
The inspector warned that the kitchen would be cleaned if it stayed closed.
wrongAf: Die inspekteur het gewaarsku dat die kombuis gesluit sou word indien dit bly vuil.
Die inspekteur het gewaarsku dat die kombuis gesluit sou word indien dit skoon bly.
Die eienaar het gewaarsku dat die kombuis gesluit sou word indien dit vuil bly.
Die inspekteur het gewaarsku dat die kombuis gesluit is omdat dit vuil was.
items.note: A reported warning with a passive in the past (gesluit sou word = would be closed). 'Indien' (if) sends 'bly' last.

items.af: Na die droogte was groente so skaars soos hoendertande, en pryse het die hoogte ingeskiet.
items.en: After the drought, vegetables were as scarce as hen's teeth, and prices shot up.
wrongEn: After the drought, vegetables were plentiful, and prices dropped.
After the drought, hens' teeth and vegetables were scarce, and prices shot up.
Before the drought, vegetables were as scarce as hen's teeth, and prices shot up.
After the drought, vegetables were as scarce as hen's teeth, yet prices stayed low.
wrongAf: Na die droogte groente was so skaars soos hoendertande, en pryse het die hoogte ingeskiet.
Na die droogte was groente so skaars soos hoendertande, en pryse het die hoogte geinskiet.
Na die droogte was groente so skaars soos hoendertande, en pryse het die laagte ingeskiet.
Na die droogte was groente volop, en pryse het gedaal.
items.note: Two idioms: 'so skaars soos hoendertande' (extremely rare) and 'die hoogte inskiet' (shoot up).

items.af: Die geur van kaneel het soos 'n onsigbare hand elke gas kombuis toe gelok.
items.en: The smell of cinnamon lured every guest to the kitchen like an invisible hand.
wrongEn: An invisible hand carried cinnamon through the house to every guest.
The smell of cinnamon drove every guest out of the kitchen like a thick fog.
The smell of cinnamon drifted away because every guest was in the kitchen.
The smell of ginger lured every guest to the garden like an invisible hand.
wrongAf: Die geur van kaneel het soos 'n onsigbare hand elke gas kombuis toe lok.
Die geur van kaneel soos 'n onsigbare hand het elke gas kombuis toe gelok.
'n Onsigbare hand het die kaneel na elke gas in die kombuis gedra.
Die geur van kaneel het soos 'n digte mis elke gas uit die kombuis verdryf.
items.note: A simile with personification: the smell acts like a hand. 'Kombuis toe' = to the kitchen; lok becomes gelok.

items.af: Ouma het nooit resepte neergeskryf nie, en niemand kon haar melktert nog ooit namaak nie.
items.en: Grandma never wrote down recipes, and nobody has ever managed to copy her milk tart.
wrongEn: Grandma always wrote down recipes, so everybody has managed to copy her milk tart.
Grandma never wrote down recipes, but somebody has managed to copy her milk tart.
Grandma never read recipes, and nobody has ever managed to copy her milk tart.
Grandma never wrote down recipes, and she never managed to copy anyone's milk tart.
wrongAf: Ouma het nooit resepte neergeskryf, en niemand kon haar melktert nog ooit namaak nie.
Ouma het nooit resepte geneerskryf nie, en niemand kon haar melktert nog ooit namaak nie.
Ouma het nooit resepte neergeskryf nie, en niemand kon haar melktert nog ooit namaak.
Ouma het altyd resepte neergeskryf, en almal kon haar melktert namaak.
items.note: Two negative clauses, each closed by its own 'nie': nooit ... nie and niemand ... nie.

items.af: Aangesien die vraag toeneem, oorweeg die supermark dit om plaaslike boere aan te stel.
items.en: Since demand is growing, the supermarket is considering taking on local farmers.
wrongEn: Since demand is falling, the supermarket is considering dropping local farmers.
Since demand is growing, the supermarket has already taken on local farmers.
Since the supermarket took on local farmers, demand has grown.
Although demand is growing, the supermarket is not considering local farmers.
wrongAf: Aangesien die vraag neem toe, oorweeg die supermark dit om plaaslike boere aan te stel.
Aangesien die vraag toeneem, die supermark oorweeg dit om plaaslike boere aan te stel.
Aangesien die vraag toeneem, oorweeg die supermark dit om plaaslike boere te aanstel.
Aangesien die vraag afneem, oorweeg die supermark dit om plaaslike boere af te dank.
items.note: Separable verbs stay whole at the end of a subordinate clause (toeneem) but split around 'te': aan te stel.
